## Theme: `theme_j2me()`

Graphs in this chapter use `ggrewindr::theme_j2me()`, built from a Nokia N73 running a J2ME app: a black phone background, a silver frame, a pale screen panel, Ushahidi red, tan, brown, and black marks, and an Archivo Narrow title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(treemapify)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
set.seed(2003)
j2me_downloads <- tibble(
  genre = c("Puzzle", "Puzzle", "Racing", "Racing",
            "Sports", "Sports"),
  title = c("Block Drop", "Gem Swap", "Street Rally", "Moto Sprint",
            "Pocket Soccer", "Pro Bowling"),
  yearly_rate = c(1800, 900, 2400, 700, 1200, 1000),
  deck_share = c(0.80, 0.40, 0.35, 0.60, 0.55, 0.50)) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(channel = c("Carrier deck", "Direct")) |>
  mutate(lambda = yearly_rate *
           if_else(channel == "Carrier deck", deck_share, 1 - deck_share),
         downloads = rpois(n(), lambda = lambda)) |>
  select(genre, title, channel, lambda, downloads)
labs_treemap <- labs(
  title = "J2ME downloads 2005",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    fill = "Channel")
ggp2_treemap <- ggplot(j2me_downloads,
       aes(area = downloads,
           fill = channel,
           label = channel,
           subgroup = genre,
           subgroup2 = title)) +
       treemapify::geom_treemap() +
       treemapify::geom_treemap_text(
           place = "bottomright",
           color = "#FFFFFF",
           min.size = 0,
           alpha = 0.90,
           fontface = "italic",
           family = "sans")
ggp2_tm_subgroup <- ggp2_treemap +
    treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border(
           color = "#15110E",
           size = 4.0) +
       treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text(
           place = "center",
           alpha = 0.75,
           color = "#FFFFFF",
           min.size = 0,
           family = "sans")
ggp2_tm_subgroup2 <- ggp2_tm_subgroup +
       treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border(
           color = "#9A9791",
           size = 4) +
       treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_text(
           place = "topleft",
           alpha = 0.65,
           grow = TRUE,
           color = "#FFFFFF",
           min.size = 0,
           family = "mono",
           fontface = "bold")

ggp2_tm_subgroup2 +
  labs_treemap
```

::: {.fm-req-title}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {.fm-req}
**✅ at least two categorical variables**
:::

::: {.fm-req}
**✅ a numeric variable of counts (for each level of the categorical variables)**
:::

::::

## Description

Treemaps display proportionally divided rectangular hierarchies for levels of categorical variables. The layout consists of 'squarified' tiles, which display the relative contribution of each categorical value to the overall graph space.

We'll build a treemap using the [`treemapify` package.](http://wilkox.org/treemapify/) Also check out the [mosaic plots](mosaic_plots.qmd) chapter.

## Set up

### PACKAGES {.unnumbered .fm-label}

Install packages.

```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_treemap
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
# pak::pak("wilkox/treemapify")
library(treemapify)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation
library(tidyr) # for expand_grid()
```



### DATA {.unnumbered .fm-label}

In the early to mid 2000s, most mobile phone games were small J2ME (Java ME) apps that a phone downloaded over the air. Most were bought from the carrier's deck (the games menu on the operator's portal). They held on until the iPhone App Store and Android Market replaced them.

We'll simulate one year of downloads for six made up titles in three genres. Each title gets a `yearly_rate` (the downloads we'd expect in a year) and a `deck_share` (the part of those downloads bought through the carrier deck instead of directly from the publisher's site). `tidyr::expand_grid()` creates a row for each title in each `channel`, `lambda` splits the yearly rate between the two channels, and `rpois()` draws the downloads. Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same downloads every time you run the code below.

```{r}
#| label: data_code_treemap
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(2003) # same downloads every time the code runs
j2me_downloads <- tibble(
  genre = c("Puzzle", "Puzzle", "Racing", "Racing", # three genres, two games each
            "Sports", "Sports"),
  title = c("Block Drop", "Gem Swap", "Street Rally", "Moto Sprint", # six games
            "Pocket Soccer", "Pro Bowling"),
  yearly_rate = c(1800, 900, 2400, 700, 1200, 1000), # average downloads per year
  deck_share = c(0.80, 0.40, 0.35, 0.60, 0.55, 0.50) # share sold through the carrier's menu
  ) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(channel = c("Carrier deck", "Direct")) |> # each game in both channels
  mutate(
    lambda = yearly_rate *
      if_else(channel == "Carrier deck", deck_share, 1 - deck_share), # average downloads in each channel
    downloads = rpois(n(), lambda = lambda) # download counts around each average
    ) |>
  select(genre, title, channel, lambda, downloads)
glimpse(j2me_downloads)
```

## Distribution

A treemap nests counts inside counts: channels inside titles, and titles inside genres. Every tile's area is a share of the total downloads, so the question behind the graph is "how much of the whole does each piece take up?" Below we'll move from the downloads, to a picture, to the formula.

### COUNT IT {.unnumbered .fm-step}

Start with the rows for Block Drop and Street Rally.

```{r}
#| label: count_values_treemap
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
j2me_downloads |>
  filter(title %in% c("Block Drop", "Street Rally"))
```

Each simulated count (`downloads`) lands within a few percent of the rate we gave `rpois()` (`lambda`). Block Drop got most of its downloads through the carrier deck, while Street Rally got most of its downloads directly. Adding up the counts inside each genre gives the genre totals, and dividing by the overall total turns them into the shares the treemap draws.

```{r}
#| label: count_summary_treemap
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
j2me_downloads |>
  group_by(genre) |>
  summarise(downloads = sum(downloads), expected = sum(lambda)) |>
  mutate(share = round(downloads / sum(downloads), 3))
```

### DRAW IT {.unnumbered .fm-step}

A bar model shows the hierarchy one level at a time. Each genre is a bar, each title is a part of its genre's bar, and each part is split by channel.

```{r}
#| label: draw_bar_model_treemap
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggplot(j2me_downloads, aes(x = downloads, y = title, fill = channel)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid(genre ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Downloads", y = NULL, fill = "Channel") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

A treemap takes the same parts and packs them into one rectangle. Below, the silver borders outline the genres, the black borders outline the titles, and the red and tan fills split each title by channel. The Block Drop tile is about four fifths carrier deck downloads, and the Street Rally tile is mostly direct downloads.

```{r}
#| label: draw_treemap
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggplot(j2me_downloads, aes(area = downloads, fill = channel,
    subgroup = genre, subgroup2 = title)) +
  treemapify::geom_treemap() +
  treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border(color = "#15110E", size = 3) +
  treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text(color = "#FFFFFF",
    place = "center", min.size = 0, family = "sans") +
  treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border(color = "#9A9791", size = 6) +
  labs(fill = "Channel") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

### NAME IT {.unnumbered .fm-step}

Each title and channel count comes from a [Poisson distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson_distribution):

$$
N_{\text{title, channel}} \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_{\text{title, channel}})
$$

Poisson counts have a useful property for treemaps: the sum of independent Poisson counts is also Poisson, with a rate equal to the sum of the rates. So each genre total is $\text{Poisson}(\sum \lambda)$: 2,700 for puzzle, 3,100 for racing, and 2,200 for sports.

The standard deviation of a Poisson count is $\sqrt{\lambda}$, so its relative wobble is $\sqrt{\lambda} / \lambda = 1 / \sqrt{\lambda}$. For the Block Drop carrier deck tile ($\lambda = 1{,}440$) that's under 3%, which is why the treemap's tiles barely change shape from one simulation to the next. Try dividing every `yearly_rate` by 100 and the small tiles start to jump around.

### CHANGE IT {.unnumbered .fm-step}

So far the treemap shows what we expect: racing is the biggest genre, and no single tile fills more than a fifth of the rectangle. Now we'll change the downloads for one title. In 2005, a game at the top of the carrier deck sold far more copies than one buried a few screens down.

Suppose a carrier moved Moto Sprint to the top of its games menu for the whole year. Its carrier deck rate grows tenfold (from 420 to 4,200). We'll draw a new count for that one tile and leave the other eleven tiles alone. Block Drop still has the same downloads, so we'd expect its tile to stay the same size, but does it?

```{r}
#| label: change_data_treemap
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(2003) # same seed as above
moto_deck <- j2me_downloads$title == "Moto Sprint" &
  j2me_downloads$channel == "Carrier deck" # the one tile we change
j2me_featured <- j2me_downloads |>
  mutate(
    lambda = if_else(moto_deck, 4200, lambda), # ten times the old rate
    downloads = if_else(moto_deck, rpois(n(), lambda), downloads) # new count for that tile only
    )
j2me_featured |>
  group_by(genre) |>
  summarise(downloads = sum(downloads)) |>
  mutate(share = round(downloads / sum(downloads), 3))
```

Below we redraw the same treemap with the new downloads.

```{r}
#| label: change_graph_treemap
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggplot(j2me_featured, aes(area = downloads, fill = channel,
    subgroup = genre, subgroup2 = title)) +
  treemapify::geom_treemap() +
  treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border(color = "#15110E", size = 3) +
  treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text(color = "#FFFFFF",
    place = "center", min.size = 0, family = "sans") +
  treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border(color = "#9A9791", size = 6) +
  labs(fill = "Channel") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: change_numbers_treemap
#| include: false
block_deck <- j2me_downloads$downloads[j2me_downloads$title == "Block Drop" &
  j2me_downloads$channel == "Carrier deck"]
block_share_before <- block_deck / sum(j2me_downloads$downloads)
block_share_after <- block_deck / sum(j2me_featured$downloads)
moto_share <- j2me_featured$downloads[moto_deck] / sum(j2me_featured$downloads)
puzzle_share_before <- sum(j2me_downloads$downloads[j2me_downloads$genre == "Puzzle"]) /
  sum(j2me_downloads$downloads)
puzzle_share_after <- sum(j2me_featured$downloads[j2me_featured$genre == "Puzzle"]) /
  sum(j2me_featured$downloads)
```

One tile now fills about a third of the rectangle. The Moto Sprint carrier deck tile holds `r format(j2me_featured$downloads[moto_deck], big.mark = ",")` downloads, or `r round(100 * moto_share)` percent of the total. Block Drop sold the same `r format(block_deck, big.mark = ",")` copies through the carrier deck, but its tile shrank from `r round(100 * block_share_before)` to `r round(100 * block_share_after)` percent of the area. The puzzle genre shrank from `r round(100 * puzzle_share_before)` to `r round(100 * puzzle_share_after)` percent and moved to a new corner.

Every tile is a share of the whole, so one big tile squeezes all the others. The graph can't tell us whether a title lost downloads or just lost space to a hit. I've found it's worth printing the totals next to a treemap (like the `downloads` column above). Then readers can tell a shrinking title from a growing neighbor.


## Grammar


### CODE {.unnumbered .fm-label}


  -   Create labels with `labs()`

  -   Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  -   Map the `downloads` to `area`, `channel` to `fill` and `label`, `genre` to `subgroup`, and `title` to `subgroup2`

  -   Add `geom_treemap()`

  -   Add `geom_treemap_text()`

      - `place`: this controls where the boxes start

      - `color`: text color

      - `min.size`: the minimum font size (when re-sizing)

      - `alpha`: opacity

      - `fontface`: `italic`/`bold`

      - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"`

```{r}
#| label: code_graph_treemap
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
labs_treemap <- labs(
  title = "J2ME downloads 2005",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    fill = "Channel")
ggp2_treemap <- ggplot(j2me_downloads,
       aes(area = downloads,
           fill = channel,
           label = channel,
           subgroup = genre,
           subgroup2 = title)) +
       treemapify::geom_treemap() +
       treemapify::geom_treemap_text(
           place = "bottomright",
           color = "#FFFFFF",
           min.size = 0,
           alpha = 0.90,
           fontface = "italic",
           family = "sans")
ggp2_treemap +
  labs_treemap
```



### GRAPH {.unnumbered .fm-label}

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_treemap
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_treemap <- labs(
  title = "J2ME downloads 2005",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    fill = "Channel")
ggp2_treemap <- ggplot(j2me_downloads,
       aes(area = downloads,
           fill = channel,
           label = channel,
           subgroup = genre,
           subgroup2 = title)) +
       treemapify::geom_treemap() +
       treemapify::geom_treemap_text(
           place = "bottomright",
           color = "#FFFFFF",
           min.size = 0,
           alpha = 0.90,
           fontface = "italic",
           family = "sans")
ggp2_treemap +
  labs_treemap
```

## More info

`treemapify` has multiple options for building treemaps. We cover a few of these below, but you should check out the [package vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/treemapify/vignettes/introduction-to-treemapify.html).

### Subgroup 2

`ggplot2` builds layers in the order they're written, so it's [advised](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/treemapify/vignettes/introduction-to-treemapify.html) to build the subgroups in order from "*from deepest to shallowest*", with `subgroup2` first (ending on `subgroup`)

- Add `geom_treemap_subgroup2_border()`

  - Set the `size` and `color`

- Add `geom_treemap_subgroup2_text()`

  - `place`: this controls where the boxes start

  - `color`: text color

  - `min.size`: the minimum font size (when re-sizing)

  - `alpha`: opacity

  - `fontface`: `italic`/`bold`

  - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"`


See full list of arguments [here](http://wilkox.org/treemapify/).

```{r}
#| label: code_graph_treemap_sgb
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
ggp2_tm_subgroup <- ggp2_treemap +
    treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border(
           color = "#15110E",
           size = 4.0) +
       treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text(
           place = "center",
           alpha = 0.75,
           color = "#FFFFFF",
           min.size = 0,
           family = "sans")
ggp2_tm_subgroup +
  labs_treemap
```

### Subgroup

  - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup_border()`

    - Set the `size` and `color`

  - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup_text()`

    - `place`: this controls where the boxes start

    - `color`: text color

    - `min.size`: the minimum font size (when re-sizing)

    - `alpha`: opacity

    - `fontface`: `italic`/`bold`

    - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"`

```{r}
#| label: code_graph_tmap_sgb_2
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
ggp2_tm_subgroup2 <- ggp2_tm_subgroup +
       treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border(
           color = "#9A9791",
           size = 4) +
       treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_text(
           place = "topleft",
           alpha = 0.65,
           grow = TRUE,
           color = "#FFFFFF",
           min.size = 0,
           family = "mono",
           fontface = "bold")

ggp2_tm_subgroup2 +
  labs_treemap
```
